label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8) that start with s/v and contain v/o early
explanation: Almost all activations (99.7% of mass) are on the <DEL> delimiter step, i.e. when the model outputs original token 0. Nearly all of them are in long sequences: L=9 holds 57% of the mass, L=8 36%, L=7 7%, and it never fires for L<=5. (phase==1)&(L>=8) alone gets 93% mass recall, but precision is only about 1%, because the feature is sparse within that envelope. Which sequences it fires on depends on the early original tokens. First token 's' gives 54% of the mass (26x lift) and 'v' 18%. The letters 'v' and 'o' at positions 1-3 also raise the rate (top example: s o v o t o y). It acts like a soft, additive score over these tokens: requiring 2 or more matches out of {orig0 in s/v, orig1-3 in v/o} gives dev F1 0.27 and mass recall 0.58. Requiring 3 or more raises precision to about 0.6 but drops recall to 7%. The largest activations come with 's' first plus several v/o tokens in positions 1-3. Long sequences with none of these tokens give tiny activations. It essentially never fires in the original phase (8 weak steps) or the copy phase, and the identity of the token just before <DEL> matters little.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig3=o (+3.85), phase=1 & out_tok=v (+3.59), orig1=v (+3.57), orig2=o (+3.57), orig0=s (+2.82), orig4=o (+2.75). Lower it: orig6=- (-3.65), phase=2 (-3.65), in_first=0 (-2.93), orig2=b (-2.50).
